t:
(a) Military Academy.—Section 4342(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking “4,000 or such higher number” and inserting “4,400 or such lower number”. 
    (b) Naval Academy.—Section 6954 of such title is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a), by striking “4,000 or such higher number” and inserting “4,400 or such lower number”; and 
        (2) in subsection (h)(1), by striking the last sentence.  
    (c) Air Force Academy.—Section 9342 of such title is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a), by striking “4,000 or such higher number” and inserting “4,400 or such lower number”; and 
        (2) in subsection (j)(1), by striking the last sentence.  
    (d) Effective Date.—The amendments made by this section shall apply with respect to academic years at the United States Military Academy, the United States Naval Academy, and the Air Force Academy after the 2007-2008 academic year.

fable.w: The section only amends the authorized cadet and midshipman strength limits at the three service academies and sets an effective date. No outside party (states, the public, experts, advisory bodies) is consulted or given a role in any federal decision, and no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue is created. There is no real tempting reading here; the text is purely a numerical and technical amendment.

qwen_block.w: This section amends statutory caps on the number of cadets at military academies. It involves internal administrative adjustments to federal institutions and does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public). The actors involved are federal agencies and the academies themselves.
qwen_block.s: Section 4342(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking “4,000 or such higher number” and inserting “4,400 or such lower number”.

opus.w: This section only amends the authorized student numbers at the Military, Naval and Air Force Academies, strikes certain sentences, and sets an effective date. No outside party (state, tribe, expert, company or the public) is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking requirement or right to sue. The phrase "such lower number" refers at most to an internal federal decision, not to participation by outsiders.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The amended text refers to "such lower number," which implies the Secretary may set enrollment caps on their own. Someone could read that as rulemaking authority. It fails because nothing here mentions regulations, comment periods, hearings, consultation or anyone outside the federal government. The section only changes the cadet and midshipman strength numbers and sets an effective date.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the statutory caps on the number of cadets at the United States Military Academy, Naval Academy, and Air Force Academy. It involves internal administrative adjustments to federal institutions and does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: Nothing. The text only changes numerical limits for academy enrollments.
Resolution: This provision amends statutory caps on the number of cadets at military academies. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties.
